title: Bubble Meadow
scene: Big soft bubbles in coral, leaf green, sky blue and sunshine yellow drift up over a clover meadow; one small finger touch pops a bubble into sparkles while a fawn watches and Linky giggles.

views.world: A wide, low clover meadow in the morning, dew shining on round leaves. At the far edge a short white Chord tower rises like a smooth plant stem with ringed nodes and a soft glow at its crown. Fawns graze in the mist, wildflowers sway, and the pale sky leaves plenty of empty space for bubbles to float.
views.details: Linky sits in the clover, a round chibi friend with a coral-red left eye, a sky-blue right eye and an arrow-smile. A white Orbi sphere with a glowing equator ring blows bubbles through a gentle ring of light. Bubbles are glossy and see-through with rainbow rims. Flat fills, thick rounded gray outlines, soft pastel palette.
views.discovery: Later scenes open with new kinds of bubbles: dusk bubbles that glow like lanterns, giant slow bubbles that split into three small ones, and round balloons that float up and open into quiet light blossoms over the tower. Each bubble sings one soft note, so a bubble storm becomes a little melody. A sleepy goodbye scene ends every play.

story: One morning, the little Orbi of the meadow blew a bubble. It was round and shiny, and it floated up, up, up. Linky reached out one finger. Pop! A shower of tiny sparkles fell on the clover. A fawn sneezed, and Linky laughed. The Orbi blew another bubble, and another, slow and soft. Linky did not grab. Linky touched each one gently, and each one sang a tiny note before it popped. Soon the whole meadow was humming. Then the sun grew warm, and everyone lay down for a rest.

title: Clover Peekaboo
lesson: Object permanence, waiting, joy of surprise
scene: A giant four-leaf clover fills the screen and a fawn's ears poke out from behind it. One tap anywhere folds the leaves open to reveal the fawn's happy face as a warm voice says peekaboo.

views.world: A sunny clover patch seen close up, with leaves as big as umbrellas, dewdrops and tiny daisies. Behind them lies a soft, blurred meadow with a few grazing fawns and the short white Chord tower far away under a pale blue sky. The camera sits at toddler eye level, so everything feels large, warm and safe.
views.details: Friends hide one at a time: a spotted fawn, Linky with red and blue eyes, a round white Orbi that blinks its coral and sky-blue eyes, sleepy Nully as a soft see-through bubble, and Itsy hugging itself. Covers are clover leaves, a white lattice blanket and a fern. Big shapes, flat colors and soft gray outlines.
views.discovery: New hiding places appear over time: a fern curtain, a puff of morning mist, a hollow log, and a white lattice blanket that an Orbi lifts. The reveal waits a little longer as the child grows, building happy suspense. A parent can add their own voice for each name, and the last friend to appear always yawns goodnight.

story: Where is the fawn? The clover is very big today. Linky looks left. Linky looks right. Something wiggles. Two soft ears peek over a leaf. The leaves open and... peekaboo! There is the fawn, with shiny eyes and a big smile. The fawn hides again. Linky waits. Linky knows the fawn is still there, even when the leaves are closed. Friends who hide are friends who come back. Peekaboo! Peekaboo! And at the end, the fawn curls up behind the clover and goes to sleep.

title: Who Says Hello?
scene: One big wild duck stands in the clover, flapping its wings mid-quack inside a soft sound ring. A tap anywhere brings the next animal waddling in to call out its own sound.

views.world: A meadow at the edge of a reed pond and a birch wood, in morning light and gentle mist. A short white Chord tower stands beyond the trees with its soft crown light. There are no fences, barns or paths: wild animals wander freely and unafraid. Lily pads, reeds and a flat sunny stone give each animal its own little stage.
views.details: Wild animals drawn round and chibi: a duck, a frog, an owl, a bee, a fawn, a woolly wild cow, a wild goat, a goose and a cricket. A white Orbi floats beside them and shows a soft sound ring when an animal calls. Linky claps with its red and blue hands. Warm greens, cream and sunflower yellow, flat fills with one shadow tone.
views.discovery: Later, new habitats join the meadow: a night wood with an owl and crickets, a rocky hill with wild goats, a pond full of frogs. A listening mode plays the sound first and the animal pops out after a pause, so the child can guess aloud with a parent. The day ends with all the animals humming one soft goodnight together.

story: Linky woke up and said hello to the meadow. Quack, said the duck. Ribbit, said the frog. Buzz, said the bee. Hoo, hoo, said the owl, who was very sleepy. Linky listened with both ears. Every friend has a voice, and every voice is a way to say hello. Linky tried to say hello like the duck. Quack! The duck tipped its head. Then the duck laughed in its own duck way, and they quacked together all morning long.

title: Clover Chimes
lesson: Sound, rhythm, high and low notes
scene: Eight wide rainbow chime stones fill the screen like stepping stones across the clover; a tap on any stone rings a soft note and a little flower blooms above it.

views.world: A flower steppe meadow in golden afternoon light, with the short white Chord tower in the distance glowing faintly as if it is listening. Butterflies drift, grass ripples in waves of wind, and the sky is warm apricot. Wide open space and gentle light make the scene feel like a quiet outdoor music room.
views.details: The chime stones are smooth, wide pebbles in coral, orange, yellow, leaf green, teal, sky blue, violet and pink, lying in a row. Linky bounces from stone to stone, and Verbi, the green triangle, taps a round drum made from a hollow log. An Orbi floats like a conductor with blinking red and blue eyes. Rounded, toy-like shapes.
views.discovery: New instruments join as the child plays: a set of log drums, a leaf rattle, a frog that croaks the low notes and birds that sing the high ones. All notes come from one gentle scale, so every tap sounds pretty. A play-along mode lets a parent tap a song while fawns dance; nothing is ever wrong.

story: The meadow was very quiet. Linky found a row of shiny stones in the grass. Linky tapped the first one. Ding! A tiny flower popped up. Linky tapped the last one. Dong! That one was low and deep, like a frog. Ding, dong, ding. A bird answered from the tree. Verbi hopped over and drummed on a log. Bum, bum. Soon the bird, the frog, Verbi and Linky made a song together. Nobody played it wrong, because every note was a friend.
wisdom: Every sound is a little song.

title: Pop-Up Basket
lesson: Cause and effect, surprise, naming toys
scene: A big woven white basket sits in the clover with its lid bouncing; one tap anywhere makes the lid fly open and a springy toy pops out, a ball, a spinning top or a wriggly bead friend.

views.world: A cozy corner of the toddler meadow under a broad shade tree whose roots curve like soft benches, with clover all around. The short white Chord tower peeks between the leaves. Afternoon sun makes dappled spots on the grass and a tiny stream murmurs nearby. Calm, warm and close, like a world the size of a picnic blanket.
views.details: The basket is woven from white lattice with coral and sky-blue ribbons. Toys: a wooden ball, a spinning top, a spring-legged Verbi, a Beadle bead chain that wriggles, a soft star-shaped Anya and a little drum. An Orbi lifts toys with a gentle shimmer. Wood, felt and woven textures in warm pastels.
views.discovery: As play grows, the basket learns new tricks: toys that hide again on a second tap, Oopsy popping out like a jack-in-the-box who laughs and tumbles over, a music toy that plays a short tune, and a goodnight mode where every toy climbs back into the basket and the lid closes softly.

story: In the shade of the big tree stood a white basket. It was very still. Then... bump! The lid jumped. Linky tapped it. Out popped a red ball! Boing, boing, it bounced away. Linky tapped again. Out popped Oopsy, with a band-aid and a big grin. Oopsy fell over and laughed. Linky laughed too. Every tap brought a new friend. When the sun went low, all the toys climbed back inside, and the lid closed with a tiny click. Goodnight, toys.

title: Hello, Little Fish
genre: Tap fishing (fish jump and say hello)
lesson: Cause and effect, colors, caring for animals
scene: A calm round pond with lily pads fills the screen; a tap anywhere on the water makes a bright fish leap from that spot in a glittering arc, wave a fin and splash back home.

views.world: A clear pond in the clover meadow, edged with reeds, round stones and forget-me-nots. A heron stands far off, and the short white Chord tower is reflected upside down in the still water. Morning light makes the ripples sparkle, and the water is clean enough to see pebbles on the bottom.
views.details: Round chibi fish in coral, gold, teal and lilac with big friendly eyes. Linky sits on a flat stone with its feet dangling. A white Orbi hovers over the water, its red and blue eyes watching, and makes a soft shimmer where the fish jump. Glossy water, matte leaves, flat fills and gentle shadows. Nobody catches or keeps a fish.
views.discovery: Later ponds bring new friends: a frog that jumps after the fish, a turtle that pops its head up, and a night pond where glowing fish draw rings of light. An Orbi bubble window lets the child peek under the water at a fish family, then the bubble pops and everyone swims on. The fish always stay in their pond.

story: Linky sat by the pond. Plip! Linky touched the water. Up jumped a little gold fish, round and shiny. It waved one fin. Hello! Splash, it went back home. Plip! A blue fish jumped. Plip! A pink fish. Linky did not try to take them. Fish love the water, and the water loves the fish. Linky just said hello, and the fish said hello back. When the sky turned pink, the fish swam to their beds under the lily pads.
wisdom: Say hello, then let them go.

title: Pim and Pom Lullaby
lesson: Calming down, bedtime, the night sky
scene: A deep blue night meadow lies under two small moons; a tap anywhere sprinkles a cluster of stars that hum one soft lullaby note, while a sleepy fawn curls up in the clover below.

views.world: The toddler meadow at night, deep blue but never black. The short white Chord tower glows softly at its crown, dimmed and shielded for the animals. Two little moons, Pim and Pom, hang over a far hill. Fireflies drift above the clover, and a river of stars fills the quiet sky.
views.details: Sleepy friends: a curled-up fawn, Linky yawning with half-closed red and blue eyes, Nully as a soft see-through nap bubble, and an Orbi floating low with dim eyes like a night light. Stars are round and soft with gentle halos. A palette of indigo, lavender, cream and moon silver.
views.discovery: Each night the sky offers a new gentle picture: fireflies that follow the finger, stars that join into the shape of a sleeping fawn, a slow shooting star that sings, and a cloud that tucks the moons in. The music slows and fades over a few minutes, the screen dims by itself, and the game always ends asleep.

story: The sun went down behind the hill. Pim came up, and then Pom, the two little moons. Linky yawned a big yawn. The fawn yawned a small yawn. Linky touched the sky, and a star came out, singing hmmm. Another star, and another, very softly. Nully floated by and whispered, rest is important. The Orbi made its light low and warm. The stars sang slower and slower. The fawn closed its eyes. Linky closed its eyes. Goodnight, Pim. Goodnight, Pom. Goodnight, meadow.

title: Clover Fingerpaint
scene: A smooth white canvas leans on a stone in the meadow; a finger swirls thick coral and leaf-green paint across it, leaving trails of little sparkles, while Linky claps beside five big round paint pots.

views.world: A breezy meadow corner beside the short white Chord tower, with smooth flat stones that stand like easels and wildflowers that inspire the colors. Soft morning light, no harsh shadows. Butterflies land near the drying paint. The background stays calm and pale, so the painting is always the brightest thing on screen.
views.details: Five huge paint pots shaped like flower cups: coral, sunshine yellow, leaf green, sky blue and violet. Linky holds up its red hand and blue hand, both covered in paint. An Orbi lifts a finished painting toward the sky with a shimmer. Thick creamy paint texture, sparkles and rounded brush trails.
views.discovery: Later, new brushes appear one by one: a clover-leaf stamp, a rainbow brush, a sparkle brush and paint that makes soft sounds as it flows. Finished paintings hang on a white lattice line in a little meadow gallery. A parent can keep a painting for the family; nothing ever leaves the device.

story: Linky found a white stone, flat and clean. Linky dipped one finger in yellow paint. Swish! A sun. Linky dipped a finger in green. Swoosh! Grass. Then Linky dipped all its fingers in blue and made a big, wiggly sky. It did not look like anything else in the world. It looked like Linky. The fawns came to look. The Orbi lifted the painting up high so the whole meadow could see. Every painting is right, because every painting is yours.

title: Choo-Choo Parade
lesson: Vehicle names and sounds, things that move
scene: Choo-Choo Seq, a cheerful train of paired friend cars, rolls across the clover toward a tiny bridge; a tap anywhere sends the next toy vehicle past with its sound, a sailboat, a bicycle or a balloon.

views.world: Omi's toy meadow, a soft play version of the clover meadow, with a curving wooden toy track, a little stream, a tiny arched bridge and a toy-sized white tower. There are no roads or cars: the vehicles are toys in a learning world. Clear midday light, puffy clouds and a gentle hill to roll down.
views.details: Choo-Choo Seq has round cars, each carrying a pair of friends: Soru in coral and Tari in sky blue. The other toy vehicles are a white sailboat on the stream, a bicycle with a bell, a hot-air balloon, a kite, a little rowing boat and a glider. Wood and felt toy textures, rounded edges and bright flat colors.
views.discovery: New vehicles join the parade over time: a slow raft, a big sailing ship and a pearl glider riding the sky-lane near the white tower. A sound guessing mode plays the sound first, then the vehicle rolls in. At the end, every vehicle parks in a row and Choo-Choo Seq says goodnight with a soft whistle.

story: Choo-choo! Here comes Seq, the train of friends. Each car carries two friends holding hands. Ring-ring! Here comes a little bicycle. Whoosh! Here comes a sailboat on the stream. Fwoo! A big round balloon floats over the hill. Linky waves at everyone. They all go somewhere different, but they all share the same meadow. At the end of the day, the train, the bike, the boat and the balloon line up in a row. One, two, three, four. Big things are made of small steps.
wisdom: Big things are made of small steps.

title: Hum-Along Hill
scene: Friends sit in a row on a grassy hill, Linky, a fawn, Verbi and an Orbi; a tap anywhere starts the next line of a short original song, and everyone sways and claps in time.

views.world: A round grassy hill in the clover meadow at sunset, with the short white Chord tower behind it glowing gently as if it hums along. The sky is warm orange, long soft shadows stretch over the grass, and the first fireflies come out. The hill feels like a little outdoor stage, open and safe.
views.details: Linky with red and blue eyes, a fawn with white spots, Verbi bouncing on springy legs, Soru and Tari holding hands, and an Orbi keeping the beat with a pulsing equator ring. Simple dance poses: clap, sway, wave and nod. A warm sunset palette of coral, peach, gold and soft green.
views.discovery: A small songbook of short original rhymes grows over time: a bubble song, a counting song with fawns, a washing song and a goodnight song. The actions match the words, so children learn to clap, wave and touch their nose together with the friends. A slow mode lets parents sing along at their own pace.

story: On the top of the hill, the friends sat in a row. Linky began to hum. Hmm, hmm. The fawn nodded. Verbi bounced. Clap, clap. The Orbi made its light blink in time. Then everybody sang the meadow song, a little song about clover and sky. Some voices were high and some were low. Some friends sang the wrong words, and nobody minded. A song is better when we sing it together. When the song was done, the sun went to bed.

title: Word Leaves
scene: One huge leaf-shaped card fills the middle of the screen showing a shiny apple; a tap on the card makes the apple bounce as a warm voice says its name, and a big leaf arrow waits for the next card.

views.world: A soft clover meadow with a picnic feeling: the cards rest on a giant round leaf like a table, the short white Chord tower stands small in the distance, and the sky is clear. Bright, even light keeps every picture easy to see. Background details are blurred and quiet so nothing competes with the card.
views.details: Picture cards show familiar things drawn simply: an apple, a ball, a cup, a shoe, a fawn, a duck, a flower, the moon, a bed, a hat, the sun and water. Each card is a big rounded leaf with a single object. Linky points with its red hand, and an Orbi glows when the word is spoken. No letters anywhere.
views.discovery: Card sets grow by theme: food, animals, home, clothes, nature, body and family words. A pointing mode shows two cards and gently asks where the duck is, and either answer is praised and named. Parents can record their own voice for a word in their language, kept only on the device.

story: Linky and the Orbi went for a walk with a basket of leaves. On each leaf was a picture. Apple, said the Orbi. Linky said, ap-pull! Ball, said the Orbi. Linky said, baw! Linky did not say every word right yet. That was fine. Words grow like clover, a tiny bit every day. By the end of the walk, Linky knew three new words. Linky whispered the best one to the fawn: friend.
wisdom: Words grow a little every day.

title: Clover Coloring
scene: A big line drawing of a fawn under a tree has only four large parts; a tap on the sky pours sky-blue paint in with a splash, while five fat paint drops wait at the bottom to pick another color.

views.world: The coloring pictures show the toddler meadow itself: clover, the short white Chord tower, fawns, bubbles and ponds, all drawn as thick, friendly line art. Around the canvas, a pale lattice frame and a calm cream background keep the focus on the picture. Gentle, even morning light.
views.details: Five huge paint drops sit at the bottom: coral, sunshine yellow, leaf green, sky blue and violet. Pictures have three to six big parts with very thick rounded outlines, so every tap lands. Linky cheers with red and blue hands when a part fills. Soft paint splash particles and a glossy finish.
views.discovery: Picture packs grow: animals, friends, the night sky and the toy parade. Parts get a little smaller as the child grows, and a magic brush fills with gentle rainbow stripes. Finished pictures come alive with a small animation, the fawn wags its tail, the bubble floats away, and they collect in a meadow album.

story: The meadow woke up without colors. The fawn was white. The sky was white. Even the clover was white! Linky picked up a drop of blue and touched the sky. Splash! The sky was blue. Linky touched the clover with green. Splash! Linky made the fawn orange with white spots. And then Linky made one cloud pink, just because. The fawn liked its new color and jumped for joy. A world is happier with everyone's colors.
wisdom: Add your color to the world.

title: Snap-Together Pictures
lesson: Parts and wholes, shapes, hand-eye coordination
scene: A picture of a duck is split into two huge pieces; one half waits inside its glowing outline while the child drags the other half close, and it snaps into place with a happy pop.

views.world: A flat sunny stone in the clover meadow works as the puzzle table, with the short white Chord tower and grazing fawns softly blurred behind it. Even light and no harsh shadows. The empty spot for each piece glows faintly, like a footprint in the grass, so the target is easy to see.
views.details: Pieces are thick rounded shapes like wooden toy puzzle pieces, cut straight into halves, thirds and quarters, never with tricky tabs. Pictures show a duck, a fawn, Linky, an Orbi, the sun and a sailboat. Snap areas are big and forgiving. Warm wood edges, bright flat colors and soft gray outlines.
views.discovery: Puzzles grow from two pieces to three and then four, and every finished picture comes alive: the duck quacks and swims away, the boat sails off. Sets cover animals, friends and toys. A finished-puzzle meadow shows every picture the child has built, all waving hello.

story: Oh no, the picture of the duck was in two parts! One part had the head. One part had the tail. Linky picked up the head and slid it, slowly, slowly, next to the tail. Click! The duck was whole again. Quack! said the duck, and it swam away across the stone. Then Linky found a picture of the fawn in three parts. Click, click, click. When parts come together, something new can happen.

title: Linky's Snack Time
scene: Linky sits on the clover with a rumbling round tummy; the child drags one big shiny apple from a leaf plate to Linky's open arrow-smile, and Linky munches with a happy wiggle.

views.world: A picnic spot under a wild apple tree in the toddler meadow, with a soft woven white blanket spread on the clover. The short white Chord tower rises behind the tree. Midday light, a few birds pecking at fallen seeds, and a calm, warm mood. Apples still hang on the branches for the birds.
views.details: All foods are plants: an apple, a pear, berries, peas, carrot coins, a slice of melon and a cup of water. A leaf plate holds two items at a time. Linky opens its arrow-smile wide; an Orbi brings food copied overnight by the home garden, glowing a little. Rounded food shapes with juicy, glossy highlights.
views.discovery: New hungry friends visit: a fawn who loves clover, a duck who loves seeds and Verbi who loves peas. Each friend says yum and thank you, and a full tummy leads to a little nap. A sharing mode lets Linky give half an apple to a friend. No sweets race, no counting, no wrong food.

story: Grumble, grumble. What was that noise? It was Linky's tummy! Linky was hungry. The Orbi brought an apple from the garden. It was a copy, made in the night, so the real apple stayed on the tree for the birds. Munch, munch. Linky smiled. Then the Orbi brought peas. Crunch, crunch. And a cup of water. Glug, glug. Linky was full. Linky saved one berry for the fawn, because food tastes better when we share.

title: Bubble Bath Buddy
lesson: Washing, body care, cause and effect
scene: A muddy fawn stands in a round wooden tub of warm water; the child rubs a big foamy cloud sponge over the brown mud spots, and they vanish under clouds of rainbow bubbles.

views.world: A sunny bath corner beside a little stream in the clover meadow, with a round wooden tub, smooth stones and a towel hanging on a white lattice frame. The short white Chord tower shines in the background. Steam curls softly above the water. Warm, clean and cheerful light.
views.details: The fawn has soft brown mud spots that shine when clean. A sponge shaped like a cloud, soap that makes rainbow bubbles, a watering can for rinsing and a fluffy towel. Linky helps with its red and blue hands, and an Orbi warms the water with a gentle glow. Foam, splash and soft cloth textures.
views.discovery: Later, other friends need a wash too: Linky, sticky after painting, a sandy duck and Verbi covered in leaves. New bath toys appear, a floating boat and a squirting frog. After the rinse comes the towel and a cozy shake, and the last bath of the day ends with pajamas and a yawn.

story: The fawn played in the mud all day. Splish, splosh! Now its legs were brown, its nose was brown, and even one ear was brown. Linky filled the tub with warm water. The Orbi made it just right, not too hot. Linky took a soft sponge and rubbed the mud away. Scrub, scrub, bubbles everywhere! Then came a splash of clean water and a big fluffy towel. The fawn shook itself and sprinkled everyone. Clean and cozy feels good.

title: Sparkly Teeth
scene: A baby otter on a river stone opens its mouth wide, showing four big teeth with fuzzy crumb spots; the child rubs a chunky toothbrush over a glowing tooth and it sparkles clean.

views.world: A calm river bend in the toddler meadow at evening, with round stones, reeds and a small waterfall. The short white Chord tower glows softly behind the willows. Warm light from an Orbi makes the riverbank feel like a cozy bathroom by the water. Peaceful, quiet and slow.
views.details: The otter is round and fluffy with big eyes and four big front teeth. A chunky toothbrush with soft blue bristles, minty bubble foam, a cup of water and a little mirror pool. Linky brushes its own arrow-smile alongside. The crumb spots look like little berry bits, never like germs with faces.
views.discovery: Other friends join the evening brush: a fawn, a beaver kit and Linky. A short brushing song plays while the teeth sparkle one by one, top, bottom, left and right. A brush-along mode lets the child brush their own teeth with the otter. The routine leads gently into bedtime.

story: Little Otter ate berries and crunchy seeds all day. Now there were crumbs on its teeth. Snack time was over, and brush time was here. Linky held the toothbrush. Up and down, round and round. Brush, brush, brush. A little song played. One tooth sparkled. Two teeth sparkled. Then all the teeth were shiny. Little Otter rinsed with a swish, swish, and smiled the biggest smile in the whole river.

title: Fawn's Nose and Toes
scene: A big friendly fawn faces the child and fills most of the screen; a tap on its nose makes it wiggle and sneeze, the nose glows gently, and a warm voice says nose.

views.world: A soft sunlit spot in the clover meadow with tall grass at the sides like curtains. The short white Chord tower stands far behind. The background is simple, the light is clear, and there is plenty of space around the fawn, so every body part is large and easy to touch.
views.details: The fawn is chibi-round with big ears, glossy eyes, a button nose, a white spotted back, a round tummy, four little hooves and a short tail. Linky copies each move, touching its own eyes and hands. An Orbi glows near the part that is named. A warm caramel, cream and clover-green palette.
views.discovery: More friends join: Linky with its red and blue hands, a duck with wings and webbed feet, and a frog with a long tongue. A where-is mode asks for a part, and any tap gets a kind answer that names what was touched. Children are invited to touch their own nose, ears and toes together with a parent.

story: This is the fawn. Where are the fawn's ears? Here! They flick and flutter. Where is the fawn's nose? Here! Achoo, a little sneeze. Where is the fawn's tummy? Here! It giggles, because it is ticklish. Where are the fawn's toes? Here, four little hooves that tap the ground. Linky touched its own eyes, its own hands and its own tummy too. Every body is a good body. And at night, every body needs a rest.
wisdom: Every body is a good body.

title: Muddy Train Wash
scene: Choo-Choo Seq's toy train cars wait, covered in mud, inside a sparkling wash arch; the child rubs a huge sponge over a car, the mud slides away, and the car shines coral and blue.

views.world: Omi's toy meadow, where a wooden toy track runs through a white lattice wash arch beside a little waterfall. The short white Chord tower stands at the back. Clear daylight and puddles that reflect the sky. The mud is soft and brown and the water is clean and bright.
views.details: Choo-Choo Seq has round cars that carry pairs of Soru and Tari. The wash tools are a big cloud sponge, a soap foamer, a rain shower from a small cloud and a warm wind from an Orbi. Mud, foam, drips and sparkle textures, with bright toy colors hiding under the mud.
views.discovery: Later, other toy vehicles roll in for a wash: the little sailboat, the bicycle and the balloon basket. The steps stay simple, soap, rinse, dry, with one big glowing tool at a time. Each clean vehicle rolls off waving, and the last wash of the day ends at the toy station for sleep.

story: Choo-choo! Seq came back from a long ride through the puddles. Splat, splat. Every car was covered in mud. Linky got the big sponge. Scrub, scrub, scrub. The soap made fluffy bubbles. Then a little cloud came by and rained clean water. Shhhhh. Then the Orbi blew a warm wind. Whoosh! Seq was shiny again, every car red and blue and bright. Thank you, said Seq, and rolled home to the station.

title: Sprout Patch
lesson: Plants need water and sun, patience
scene: Three big seed bumps sit in dark soil at the edge of the meadow; the child taps the one that wiggles, a soft rain cloud waters it, and a flower pops up and opens its petals.

views.world: A small wild garden at the edge of the clover meadow, with perennial plants that look natural, no fences and no rows. The short white Chord tower stands tall nearby, its solar skin glinting. Bees buzz, the morning light is warm, and a gentle shower now and then leaves a rainbow.
views.details: Seeds grow into a sunflower, a tulip, a pea vine, a strawberry plant and a tiny apple tree. A small rain cloud with a happy face, a peeking sun, and Akoren, the glowing acorn, who smiles at each sprout. Linky waits with its red and blue hands on its cheeks. Soil, leaf and petal textures.
views.discovery: The garden grows across days: plants stay where they were planted, bees and butterflies visit, and the strawberry plant shares a berry with a fawn. New kinds of seeds arrive with the seasons. A gentle evening mode lets the garden fall asleep with its petals closing. Nothing ever wilts or dies.

story: Akoren gave Linky a tiny seed. It was very small. Linky put it in the soil and waited. Nothing happened. The little cloud came and rained. Pitter, patter. The sun came out. Then, a tiny green leaf! Linky clapped. The next day there were two leaves. Then a stem. Then, one morning, a big yellow sunflower looked up at the sun. Akoren laughed slowly. Every big thing starts small.
wisdom: Big trees grow from tiny acorns.

title: Tiny White Tower
scene: A short tower of big rounded white blocks rises on the clover; the child drags one more ringed block to the top, it snaps on with a wobble, and the little tower glows at its crown.

views.world: The toddler meadow right beside the real short white Chord tower, so the toy tower copies it. Soft afternoon light, a few fawns watching and bubbles drifting by. The ground is flat, soft clover. When a tower tips, the blocks bounce gently into the grass like soft cushions.
views.details: Blocks are chunky, rounded and soft-looking, white with coral, leaf-green and sky-blue ring stripes like the nodes of a Chord tower. Linky stacks with its red and blue hands, and Oopsy giggles when the tower tumbles. An Orbi lifts the crown block for a sparkly finish. Matte, toy-like material.
views.discovery: Later, new pieces arrive: round blocks that roll, tall thin blocks, a crown block that lights up and friends who like to sit on top. A soft tumble is part of the fun, with laughter and a fresh start. A bigger building spot lets the child build two towers and link them with a glowing thread.

story: Linky wanted to build a tower just like the big white one. One block. Two blocks. Three blocks. Wobble, wobble... bump! The blocks rolled into the clover. Oopsy laughed. Oops means you're learning! Linky tried again, slower this time, big blocks at the bottom and small blocks on top. One, two, three, four, five. The little tower stood tall, and Linky put the glowing crown on top. The big tower blinked its light, as if to say hello.

title: Where's Orbi?
scene: Three big round bushes stand in the meadow; one rustles and a white glowing curve peeks out. A tap on the wiggling bush makes the Orbi pop up with blinking red and blue eyes.

views.world: A gently hilly part of the clover meadow with big round bushes, a hollow log, a mossy rock and a cluster of tall ferns. The short white Chord tower watches from the hilltop. Late afternoon light, long soft shadows and birdsong. Every hiding place is big and easy to tap.
views.details: The Orbi is a smooth white sphere about the size of a ball, with a soft equator ring, a coral-red left eye and a sky-blue right eye. Linky and a fawn take turns hiding too. Bushes shake, leaves flutter and little sparkles leak out as hints. Soft greens, mossy browns and clean white.
views.discovery: As the child grows, the hiding spots grow from two to four, and the hints get gentler: a tiny giggle, a tail sticking out, a little glow. Turns switch so the child can choose where Linky hides while the Orbi pretends to search. A wrong guess just shows a sleepy beetle who says hi.

story: Let's play hide and seek, said Linky. The Orbi closed its eyes. One, two, three! Linky ran behind a bush. But Linky's blue hand stuck out. Found you! said the Orbi. Now it was the Orbi's turn. Where was the Orbi? Not behind the log. Not behind the rock. A bush wiggled and glowed. Peek! There it was. Hiding is fun, but being found is even better, because then you are together again.
wisdom: Being found is the best part.

title: Goodnight Nest
scene: Linky sits in a cozy white lattice nest in a tree at dusk; one big glowing item waits, soft pajamas, and a tap puts them on with a gentle whoosh before the next step lights up.

views.world: A cozy nest woven from white lattice and grown wood, high in a blue-green tree at the edge of the clover meadow. The short white Chord tower glows softly nearby. Dusk turns the sky lavender, fireflies come out, and the round window of the nest shows Pim and Pom rising.
views.details: Each step is one big glowing object: a bath cup, soft pajamas, a toothbrush, a picture book, a cuddly plush fawn and a night light. Linky yawns with sleepy red and blue eyes, and an Orbi dims to a warm glow. Soft felt, knitted blanket and wood textures in lavender and honey colors.
views.discovery: Over time a parent can arrange the same steps to match the family's own evening. Friends join the nest: the fawn, Nully, and Itsy, who gives a goodnight hug. Each night ends with the lights fading slowly and the game closing by itself, never with a cliffhanger.

story: The sky turned purple. Time for bed, little Linky. First, a warm bath. Splash. Then soft pajamas. Snuggle. Then brush, brush, brush. Then a story about a fawn who found a star. Itsy gave Linky a big hug. The Orbi made its light small and golden. Linky got under the blanket, and the nest rocked gently in the tree. Outside, Pim and Pom were shining. Every evening, the same little steps, and then sweet dreams.
wisdom: Little steps lead to sweet dreams.

title: Shape Friends Sorter
scene: A white lattice box sits in the clover with a round, a square and a triangle hole; the child drags a coral circle toward the round hole and it drops in with a happy boop.

views.world: A sunny play corner of the toddler meadow on a flat mossy rock, with the short white Chord tower behind it and a few fawns nibbling clover. Soft, even light makes the holes clear and easy to see. Everything is big, rounded and close to the camera.
views.details: The shapes follow the roles of the Links: Soru is the round coral shape, Tari the square sky-blue shape and Verbi the leaf-green triangle. Each shape has a little face. The sorter box is smooth white with glowing hole rims. A shape at the wrong hole slides back with a wiggle and a giggle.
views.discovery: Later the box grows a star hole for Anya, a heart and an oval, and the shapes change colors so the child sorts by shape, not by color. A picture mode lets shapes fill the outline of a house, a sun or a boat. When every shape is home, the box opens and the friends hug.

story: Soru is round, like a ball. Tari is square, like a box. Verbi is a triangle, like a little roof. They all wanted to go into the white box. Soru tried the square door. Bump! It did not fit. Soru tried the round door. Boop! In it went. Tari found the square door. Verbi found the triangle door. Everybody fits somewhere. You just have to find your own door.

title: Rain or Shine Closet
scene: Linky stands in the meadow under a gray rain cloud with two big clothing choices floating beside it, a rain hood and a sun hat; the child drags the rain hood onto Linky as drops patter.

views.world: The clover meadow changes weather in front of the child: a sunny morning, a soft rain shower, a windy afternoon and a snowy evening. The short white Chord tower stands in every scene. Each kind of weather is gentle and pretty, never stormy, and a rainbow always follows the rain.
views.details: The clothes are small, cute white lattice pieces with role-color accents: a rain shell hood, a sun hat, a warm scarf, mittens, boots and a wind jacket. Linky's round body wears them, and an Orbi holds an umbrella of light. Raindrops, snowflakes, wind-blown leaves and sun rays.
views.discovery: More weather and friends join: the fawn needs boots for puddles, and the duck happily needs nothing in the rain. Later, the child dresses Linky for two weather changes in one walk. Every choice is allowed and gently named; a sun hat in the rain just makes the fawn giggle and the rain hood floats closer.

story: Linky wanted to go for a walk. Pitter, patter. It was raining! Should Linky wear the sun hat or the rain hood? The rain hood! Linky stayed dry and jumped in puddles. Then the sun came out. Hot, hot! Linky put on the sun hat. In the evening, snowflakes fell. Brrr! A scarf and mittens. The sky changes, and we can change too. Linky was ready for every kind of day.
wisdom: Be ready for every kind of day.

title: Big Fawn, Little Fawn
scene: Two apples float over the clover, one big and one tiny; a mother deer and her little fawn wait below, and the child taps the tiny apple for the fawn, who bounces happily.

views.world: A sunny meadow slope below the short white Chord tower, with big trees and small bushes side by side, a big stone and a pebble, a big cloud and a tiny cloud, so the whole place plays with size. Calm light and clear space make each pair easy to compare.
views.details: Pairs of objects in big and small: apples, balls, hats, beds, boots, leaves and boats. A grown deer and a spotted fawn, a big duck and a duckling, Linky and a tiny Beadle. The sizes differ a lot, so the choice is always clear. An Orbi grows and shrinks things with a shimmer.
views.discovery: Later, three sizes appear for a big, middle and small family, like nesting cups, and the child lines them up. A grow and shrink mode lets the child tap to make things bigger or smaller with funny sounds. Every choice is named kindly, and the right fit gets a happy dance.

story: Mama Deer is big. Little Fawn is small. Mama Deer has a big bed of soft leaves. Little Fawn has a small bed. Mama Deer eats a big apple. Little Fawn eats a small one. One day Little Fawn tried on Mama's big hat. It covered its whole face! Everybody laughed. Big is good and small is good. Each size is just right for someone.
wisdom: Big or small, each one is right.

title: Color Baskets
scene: Three big woven baskets, coral, yellow and sky blue, sit in the clover; the child drags a round blue pebble into the blue basket and it plops in with a cheerful sparkle.

views.world: A corner of the wild garden by the meadow, with berry bushes, flowers and the short white Chord tower in the soft background. Late summer light, warm and golden. Everything grows wild, and the things to sort are fallen treasures blown by the wind, never picked from living plants.
views.details: Things to sort: fallen leaves, petals, pebbles, feathers, toy balls and copied berries in coral, sunshine yellow, leaf green and sky blue. The baskets are white lattice with one big color band each. Soru and Tari cheer from the basket rims. Each color also has its own shape, so color is never the only clue.
views.discovery: Sorting grows from two colors to three and four, then to light and dark, then to mixing two paints into a new color basket. A tidy-up mode puts toys back into colored boxes at the end of play. No timer and no score; every finished sort makes the baskets sing.

story: The wind blew and blew. Leaves and petals and pebbles tumbled across the meadow. What a jumble! Linky found three baskets: red, yellow and blue. A red petal went into the red basket. A yellow leaf went into the yellow basket. A blue pebble went into the blue basket. Soon everything was in its place. The meadow looked neat and bright, and the wind said sorry with a soft whoosh.

title: Who Is My Mama?
scene: A fluffy duckling stands in the clover, peeping; two grown animals wait nearby, a duck and a deer, and the child drags the duckling to the duck, who wraps it in a wing.

views.world: A peaceful meadow with a pond, a birch grove and a gentle hill below the short white Chord tower. Late afternoon warmth, with wild animals resting together in families. Nature fills the whole frame: reeds, clover, wildflowers and soft clouds.
views.details: Families: duck and duckling, deer and fawn, owl and owlet, otter and pup, goose and gosling, wild horse and foal. The babies are round, fluffy and wide-eyed. An Orbi carries a sleepy baby gently in its field. Reunions show hugs, nuzzles and wing wraps, never sad crying.
views.discovery: Families grow from two choices to three and four, and new homes appear, a nest, a burrow, a pond and a tree hollow, so the child can bring each family home. A sound mode lets a baby call and its mama answer. A goodnight scene shows every family asleep together.

story: A little duckling was playing in the clover and wandered too far. Peep, peep! Where is my mama? The fawn said, I am not your mama, my mama is the deer. The owlet said, I am not your mama, my mama is the owl. Linky picked up the duckling, very gently. Quack! called a voice from the pond. Mama Duck! The duckling ran under her wing. Everyone has someone who loves them.
wisdom: No one is lost for long.

title: Shadow Friends
scene: On a sunlit white lattice screen three soft gray shadows wait, a duck, a ball and a fawn; the child drags a bright yellow duck onto the duck shadow and it fills with color.

views.world: Golden late afternoon in the clover meadow, when long soft shadows stretch across the grass from the short white Chord tower and the trees. A smooth white lattice screen stands in the clover like a little shadow theater. Warm amber light and a calm mood.
views.details: Objects and friends with clear outlines: a duck, a fawn, Linky, an Orbi, an apple, a sailboat, a star and Verbi. The shadows are soft gray, never black, with rounded edges. When matched, a shadow turns into the colored friend, who waves. Big outlines and forgiving snap zones.
views.discovery: Later, shadows get trickier in gentle steps: three choices, then four, then shadows that wiggle, then a shadow puppet mode where the Orbi's light makes friends grow and shrink on the screen. Every Link character passes the silhouette test, so the cast itself becomes the puzzle.

story: In the evening sun, Linky saw shadows on the white screen. A shadow with long ears. A shadow with a round body. A shadow with a flat beak. Whose shadows were they? Linky held up the duck. The flat beak matched! Linky found the fawn. The long ears matched! And the round shadow? That was Linky's own shadow, waving back. Everyone has a shadow, and it goes wherever you go.
wisdom: Look closely, and you will see.

title: One, Two, Three Fawns
scene: Three fawns stand in a row in the clover; the child taps each fawn, it hops, and a warm voice counts one, two, three as three glowing dots light up in the sky.

views.world: A wide, gentle meadow in the morning with the short white Chord tower, a pond and an apple tree. Things come in small groups everywhere: two ducks, three flowers, one cloud. Clear light and empty space between the groups make every amount easy to see at a glance.
views.details: Fawns, ducks, apples, bubbles and Beadles, the bead-chain friends, where the Beadle of Three has three beads. Objects are big and spaced apart. Amounts are shown with glowing dots, never written numerals. Linky holds up fingers on its red and blue hands. A soft pastel palette.
views.discovery: Counting grows from one and two to three, then to choosing which of two baskets holds three apples. A feed-the-friends mode asks the child to give two berries to a fawn. Later, groups go up to five. Every count is voiced together, and a miscount is simply counted again together.

story: One fawn came to the pond. Hello, one! Then another fawn came. One, two! Two fawns. Then a tiny fawn came running and slipped in the clover. Oops! One, two, three. Three fawns! The Beadle of Three wiggled its three beads. Me too! Linky counted on its fingers. One, two, three. Then the fawns ran off to play, one, two, three, and Linky waved three times.
wisdom: Count with me: one, two, three.

title: Feelings Mirror
scene: A round pond mirror shows Linky's face looking happy; below it float two big face bubbles, happy and sleepy, and the child taps happy, so Linky laughs and the pond sparkles.

views.world: A still, clear pond in the clover meadow that works like a gentle mirror, ringed with smooth white stones. The short white Chord tower is reflected in the water. Soft morning light, a breeze that ripples the surface now and then, and birdsong. Calm and safe.
views.details: Linky shows big, readable feelings with its red and blue eyes and arrow-smile: happy, sad, surprised, sleepy, cross, and scared then comforted. The face bubbles are big round icons. An Orbi offers an optional mirror that shows the child's own face in the pond, on the device only and never saved.
views.discovery: Later, more friends show feelings, a fawn, a duck and Oopsy, and the child chooses among three faces. Little scenes ask how a friend feels when a balloon floats away or when a friend gets a hug. A parent-only mirror mode lets the child make faces together with Linky. Sad feelings always end comforted.

story: Linky looked into the pond. A face looked back. Linky smiled, and the face smiled. Then Linky made a sad face, because a bubble had popped. The face in the pond was sad too. Then the fawn came and nuzzled Linky. Linky's face changed into a little smile. Feelings come and go, like ripples on the water. All feelings are okay, and a friend can help a sad feeling feel better.
